title: Causal matrix Robin existence and regularity
reviewed_arguments: C0 states the precise uniformly smooth scalar Lorentz principal model with arbitrary complex matrix lower terms, zero past, restriction Hs interior forcing for every real s>=0, and the actual homogeneous Dirichlet or Robin domain. It makes no arbitrary-natural-dual existence claim.

C1 expands the complete formal adjoint and signed Green form. Bare solution Neumann data requires an adjoint matrix Robin test condition. An ordered boundary-identity test gauge removes that condition, retaining every matrix product, time derivative and lower coefficient. Uniform partial Fourier decay survives.

C2 obtains the backward small-slab estimate from the existing full matrix tangent-current proof. Reversed initial flux has the correct sign and the exponential weight is uniformly comparable to one on the slab.

C3 proves the full relative one-sided multiplier difference estimate and both Schur kernel bounds in matrix norm. The commutator is first order after conjugation, including normal-tangential derivatives. Anticausal restriction uses zero extension of actual L2 first derivatives, without differentiating a zero extension. Small-slab absorption gives the adjoint-domain estimate at every real tangential order.

C4 makes one bounded functional on the actual adjoint image. Complex Hahn-Banach and one Hilbert representation produce a supported vector distribution without closed-range or surjectivity assumptions. Interior tests establish the equation across the initial time, without an initial delta source.

C5 applies the proved finite-matrix differential normal recovery theorem with all three indices checked. The actual positive and graph traces satisfy the full rough Green identity. Explicit legal adjoint tests realize arbitrary boundary values or normal derivatives and recover the original boundary condition after undoing the full solution gauge.

C6 builds near-constant agreement models while preserving the exact normal block and Lorentz margins. Local uniqueness glues dependence regions and proves finite propagation before spatial compactness is used. Interior-centered cones meeting the physical face use separate boundary-preserving localization cutoffs.

C7 retains the complete smooth temporal cutoff residual in the original source class and exact domain. Finitely many fixed-order slabs reach each finite target time. The compact-manifold statement is conditional on a cover by the stated normalized models with one common time; it imports no unproved coordinate theorem.

C8 completes each finite-time solution at every Sobolev order before uniqueness identifies the solutions. A Fourier proof of Sobolev embedding gives smoothness up to the boundary. Exact smooth boundary lifts and a cutoff placed in a smooth past band give smooth residual correction and local regularity.

Three solved exercises check a nonzero constant adjoint Robin coefficient, every term of a time-dependent noncommuting nilpotent test gauge, and the exact continuation error. The figure shows exact gauge and smooth cutoff profiles; it is not a computed PDE solution.

Thirteen local entries bind to 737 earlier entries in 35 current maps, including 102 explicitly external Lebl proofs. Stable incoming-plus-boundary representation, sharp general Airy energy mapping and strict propagation remain unfinished; internal export P514 closure is not claimed.
